reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Definition of board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2). Defines "board" as the state board of mediation.

headings.title: Definition of collective bargaining
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2). Defines "collective bargaining" as employee bargaining through chosen representatives, including consultation and bargaining on exceptional and routine wages, hours, rules, and working conditions.

headings.title: Definition of employee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2). Defines "employee" as anyone in another's service actually engaged in or connected with operating any Missouri public utility.

headings.title: Definition of labor dispute
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2). Defines "labor dispute" as any controversy between employer and employees over hours, wages, and working conditions, noting amicable employer relations do not preclude a representation dispute among employees.

headings.title: Definition of person
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2). Defines "person" broadly to include individuals, business entities, municipal corporations, associations, and their trustees, receivers, assignees, or personal representatives.

headings.title: Definition of public utility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2). Defines "public utility" to include any person furnishing electric light or power, heat, gas, steam, water, sewer service, transportation (expressly excepting railroads), or communication to Missourians.

headings.title: Definition of representative
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2). Defines "representative" as any person, labor union, organization, or corporation designated by a utility, utility group, or its employees to act for them.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 2) and verified all fingerprints. Verified chapter 295 definitions of board, collective bargaining, employee, labor dispute, person, public utility (expressly excepting railroads), and representative. Retained all 7 drafted titles.

headings.title: Appointment, composition, and chairman of mediation board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 3). Directs governor appointment with senate consent, within 30 days of chapter effective date, of a five-member state board of mediation: two employer representatives, two bona fide union-member employees, and one neutral chairman who is neither employer nor employee.

headings.title: Staggered initial terms and three-year successor terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 3). Sets staggered initial terms (two for one year, two for two years, one for three years) and three-year terms thereafter or until successors are appointed.

headings.title: Filling board vacancies for unexpired terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 3). Directs the governor to fill any board vacancy with a competent person holding the same qualifications as the predecessor for the unexpired term.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 3) and verified all fingerprints. Verified five-member senate-confirmed state board of mediation composition and neutral chairman in sub 1, staggered initial and three-year successor terms in sub 2, and filling unexpired vacancies with same-qualified successors in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Hiring conciliators and assistants and procedural regulations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 7). Empowers the state board of mediation to employ, compensate, and delegate necessary powers to conciliators and assistants, and directs the board to prescribe procedural methods by regulation.

headings.title: Subpoena authority and circuit court contempt enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 7). Grants the board subpoena power for witnesses and evidence in matters under investigation, enforceable upon board application by Cole County or local circuit-court order punishable as contempt.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 7) and verified all fingerprints. Verified conciliator/assistant employment, delegation, and procedural regulations in sub 1 and subpoena power enforceable via Cole County or local circuit-court contempt in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Keeping board advised of labor dispute negotiations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 8). Requires the board, upon notice of a covered labor dispute, to require the parties to keep it advised of negotiation progress.

headings.title: Board conferences and settlement assistance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 8). Authorizes the board, on a party's application or its own motion, to schedule a dispute conference and take expedient steps toward settlement, including helping negotiate and draft a settlement agreement.

headings.title: Party duty to attend and remain in conferences
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 8). Imposes a duty on all parties to a labor dispute to answer board summonses for joint or separate conferences and remain until excused by the board or its representative.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 8) and verified all fingerprints. Verified keeping the board advised of dispute negotiations in sub 1, scheduling conferences and assisting settlements in sub 2, and party duty to attend and remain until excused in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Sixty-day change notice for agreements terminating after seventy days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 11). For existing labor agreements lacking a 60-day notice clause and terminating more than 70 days after chapter 295's effective date, requires written notice of desired changes to the other party and filing a copy with the state board of mediation at least 60 days before termination.

headings.title: Ten-day change notice for agreements terminating within seventy days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 11). For labor agreements terminating within 70 days after chapter 295's effective date, requires written notice of desired changes forthwith (or within 10 days of effective date) and prompt filing of demands with the state board of mediation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 11) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 60-day written change notice and board filing for existing agreements lacking a 60-day clause and terminating after 70 days from effective date in sub 1, and forthwith/10-day written change notice and board filing for agreements terminating within 70 days in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Designating three-member public hearing panel after contract expiration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 14). If utility management and employee representatives have neither executed a final written agreement nor agreed to arbitrate by contract termination, requires each side within five days to designate and file one public hearing panel member with the board, with those two choosing a disinterested third member.

headings.title: Fifteen-day hearing window, notice, and nonappearance jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 14). Requires the panel to complete public hearings on requested contract changes within 15 days of designation (extendable by mutual written consent) with full notice and opportunity to be heard, retaining jurisdiction to hear and report even if a party fails to appear.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 14) and verified all fingerprints. Verified five-day designation of a three-member public hearing panel when no final written agreement or arbitration agreement is reached by contract termination in sub 1, and 15-day extendable public-hearing window, notice, and jurisdiction despite nonappearance in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Board appointment when one party or panelists fail to choose
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 18). Directs the state board of mediation to appoint qualified employer, employee, or public panel member(s) if either side fails to designate/file or the two designees fail to choose a third member within 10 days after contract termination.

headings.title: Board panel appointment from lists when both parties default
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 18). If both management and employee representatives fail to timely designate panel members, directs the board to appoint a three-member panel (giving each side 48 hours to pick a preference from a five-person list, plus an impartial third member), proceeding even if a party fails to select.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 18) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 10-day board appointment upon single-party or panelist failure to designate/agree/file in sub 1 and board panel appointment using five-person lists with 48-hour selection windows when both parties default in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Gubernatorial seizure and operation of public utilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 19; case annotations: Rider v. Julian (1955), State v. Division 1287 (1962), Division 1287 v. State of Missouri, 83 S.Ct. 1657 (1963), and State ex rel. Rogers v. Kirtley, 372 S.W.2d 86 (1963)). Describes archived statutory text authorizing the governor to seize a utility plant, equipment, or facility for state operation during threatened or actual labor interruptions. Source annotations explicitly note the U.S. Supreme Court held the King-Thompson seizure provisions invalid under the Supremacy Clause; title describes archived text without implying current enforceability.

headings.title: Proclamation procedure, agency operation, and return after settlement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1947 enactment and 1955-1963 annotations including Division 1287 v. State of Missouri, 83 S.Ct. 1657, and State ex rel. Rogers v. Kirtley, 372 S.W.2d 86, holding seizure provisions unconstitutional under the Supremacy Clause). Describes archived text governing gubernatorial investigation, proclamation, operation through a designated agency, return of seized property as soon as practicable after settlement, and the utility's duty to resume franchised operation; describes archived text without implying current enforceability.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and all source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 19 and all four annotations: Rider v. Julian, 282 S.W.2d 484 (1955); State v. Division 1287, 361 S.W.2d 33 (1962); Division 1287 v. State of Missouri, 83 S.Ct. 1657 (1963), holding King-Thompson utility seizure invalid under the Supremacy Clause; and State ex rel. Rogers v. Kirtley, 372 S.W.2d 86 (1963)) and verified all fingerprints. Revised sub 1 title to 'Gubernatorial seizure and operation of public utilities' (removing 'authority') and retained sub 2 as strictly neutral archived-text descriptions without implying current enforceability.

headings.title: Prohibition on strikes after state takeover of utility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 21). Describes archived statutory text making it unlawful to call, incite, support, or participate in a strike or concerted work refusal after state takeover of a utility under chapter 295; note related Supremacy Clause invalidation of chapter 295 utility seizure annotated under section 295.180 (Division 1287 v. State of Missouri, 83 S.Ct. 1657).

headings.title: Re-employment of subsection 1 strikers only as new employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 21). Describes archived text making it unlawful for a public utility to employ any person who violated subsection 1 except as a new employee (subject to context of related chapter 295 seizure annotations under section 295.180).

headings.title: Daily civil forfeiture by unions for subsection 1 strikes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 21). Describes archived text imposing a $10,000-per-day civil forfeiture payable to the state for the public school fund on any labor organization or union causing a work stoppage in violation of subsection 1 (post-takeover strikes); does not imply current enforceability given the Supremacy Clause seizure annotations under section 295.180.

headings.title: Civil forfeiture by union officers for subsection 1 strikes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 21). Describes archived text imposing a $1,000 civil forfeiture payable to the state for the public school fund on any public-utility union officer participating in calling, inciting, or supporting a subsection 1 (post-takeover) strike; does not imply current enforceability given the Supremacy Clause seizure annotations under section 295.180.

headings.title: Utility lockout forfeiture and refusal-to-bargain PSC sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 21). Describes archived text imposing a $10,000-per-day civil forfeiture (for the public school fund) on a public utility causing a work stoppage by lockout, and empowering the Public Service Commission—upon board certification of refusal to bargain collectively in good faith—to revoke the utility's certificate or impose other conditions subject to judicial review; neutral archived-text description without implying current enforceability.

headings.title: Court injunctive and equitable enforcement of chapter and rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 21). Describes archived text empowering Missouri courts to enforce chapter 295 and gubernatorial rules or regulations by injunction or other legal or equitable remedies; neutral archived-text description without implying current enforceability.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections and source notes (L. 1947 V. I p. 358 § 21) and verified all fingerprints. Checked post-takeover strike prohibition in sub 1, seizure-dependent re-employment restriction and union/officer civil forfeitures expressly tied to subsection 1 in subs 2-4, utility lockout forfeiture and board-certified refusal-to-bargain PSC sanctions with judicial review in sub 5, and court injunctive/equitable enforcement in sub 6. Revised subs 2-4 titles to preserve the explicit 'subsection 1' cross-reference to post-takeover strikes and retained subs 1, 5, and 6 as neutral archived-text descriptions noting the related Supremacy Clause seizure annotations under section 295.180 without implying current enforceability.
